Recycle a Single Point Against Parameters That Vary by Observation

Source: R/generics.R
recycle_point.Rd

Checks that x and the parameters are conformable and returns x repeated to the common length when it has length one and some parameter is longer.

Usage

recycle_point(distrib, x, theta, arg = "y")

Arguments

distrib

A distrib object.

x

The response, quantile or probability, a numeric vector.

theta

The aligned parameter list.

arg

The name of x in the calling generic, used in the error message. Defaults to "y".

Value

A numeric vector.

Details

distrib_pdf(), distrib_cdf() and distrib_quantile() call it before dispatch, as the derivative generics call check_derivative_args(), and the rule is the same: with \(n\) the largest of the lengths of x and of the parameters, every parameter must have length 1 or \(n\) and x must have length 1 or \(n\); otherwise the function signals an error. A compiled kernel sizes its output by the length of the response, so a single point evaluated at parameters of length \(n\) has to be repeated \(n\) times to give one value per observation. This matters wherever a wrapper evaluates its parent at a fixed point, as zero_inflated() does for \(f(0)\). An empty x with parameters of length at most one is returned as it is. A multivariate response is a matrix and is left alone.

See also

check_derivative_args(), the derivative generics' counterpart.
